title: Aroused Savoy Forms Volunteer Fire Force At Mass Meeting
text:
Aroused Savoy Forms Volunteer Fire Force At Mass Meeting

By JOHN CLIFT
(Herald State Editor)

SAVOY, Tex. — Aroused citizens here formed a volunteer fire department in a mass meeting held at the school house Monday night, just a day after fire destroyed the Church of Christ here in a blaze that threatened the entire town.

Joe Houle, a Yankee GI who married a Savoy girl, was named fire chief after it was learned he had been a member of a New York fire department before coming here.

Glenn McKinney was named lieutenant and Holly Doan was appointed secretary.

A 7-man ways and means committee was appointed to come up with a means of financing the purchase of fire fighting equipment. Bibby was named chairman with Alton Winkler, Jim Malone, Thomas DeLerry, Dave Pritchett, Claud Strickland and W. E. Holagan as members. Holigan, incidentally, is pastor of the church that burned.

"The people of Savoy are really aroused this time to the need of adequate fire protection," said S. A. Bibby, mayor, who pointed out to the citizens that it had been as high Sunday as it was a day earlier, out entire town could have been wiped out by the fire.

Some of the many faults that occurred were brought out at the meeting. One was the failure to check fire hydrants at intervals. Two wrenches were broken trying to get one hydrant open and firemen were never able to turn on another.

It was also pointed out that the Savoy water tank was no more than two-thirds full at the time of the fire.

And city officials admitted they "hadn't gotten to it yet" when asked if the town's new 60,000 gallon storage tank had been connected.

Savoy actually has a total of 105,000 gallon storage capacity, al-though probably no more than 20,000 gallons was available Sunday morning. In addition to the 35,000 gallon main tank, it has a 10,000 gallon elevated tank and then the 60,000 gallon new tank.

Mayor Bibby said the 60,000 gallon tank will be used for "emergency storage," since the existing tanks were "adequate" when kept at a maximum level.
